claims.claim: In scikit-learn 1.8, OneHotEncoder defaults to handle_unknown="error" and ColumnTransformer to remainder="drop".
claims.source: scikit-learn 1.8 API reference; signatures checked on 1.8.0 and 1.9.1 in this repository.

concept_html:
Lesson B10-L2 fitted preprocessing on training rows by hand. scikit-learn's Pipeline does it for you, every time, including inside each cross-validation fold. Examples use scikit-learn 1.8.

A Pipeline chains steps. Calling fit fits each step on the training rows and passes its output to the next. Calling predict runs the fitted steps on new rows without refitting. Cross-validation, grid search and cross_val_score all refit the whole pipeline per fold, so no fold's test rows leak into its preprocessing.

A ColumnTransformer applies different preprocessing to different columns:

prep = ColumnTransformer([
    ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), NUMERIC),
    ("cat", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent"),
                          OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")), CATEGORICAL),
])
model = Pipeline([("prep", prep), ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])

Three defaults to know:

  • OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="error") is the default. A region that did not appear in training raises ValueError at prediction time. Set handle_unknown="ignore" to encode it as all zeros.
  • ColumnTransformer(remainder="drop") is the default. Columns you do not list are silently dropped. List every column you mean to use, or set remainder="passthrough" on purpose.
  • Output feature names come from get_feature_names_out(), prefixed with the step name: num__age, cat__region_n.

Keep the column lists in config (lesson A1-L3), and have one function build the pipeline. The same fitted object is what you save, test and deploy, so preprocessing in production is exactly what was validated.

lines: from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline, make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler
def build_pipeline(numeric: list[str], categorical: list[str]) -> Pipeline:
"""Preprocessing and model as one object, fitted per fold by CV."""
prep = ColumnTransformer(
[
("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), numeric),
(
"cat",
make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent"), OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),
categorical,
),
]
)
return Pipeline([("prep", prep), ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])

exercises.solution:
from sklearn.compose import ColumnTransformer
from sklearn.impute import SimpleImputer
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from sklearn.pipeline import Pipeline, make_pipeline
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder, StandardScaler


def build_pipeline(numeric: list[str], categorical: list[str]) -> Pipeline:
    """Preprocessing and classifier as one estimator.

    Args:
        numeric: Numeric feature columns.
        categorical: Categorical feature columns.

    Returns:
        An unfitted Pipeline with steps prep and clf.
    """
    prep = ColumnTransformer(
        [
            ("num", make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="median"), StandardScaler()), numeric),
            (
                "cat",
                make_pipeline(SimpleImputer(strategy="most_frequent"), OneHotEncoder(handle_unknown="ignore")),
                categorical,
            ),
        ]
    )
    return Pipeline([("prep", prep), ("clf", LogisticRegression(max_iter=1000))])

title: Pipeline and ColumnTransformer
why_html:
A lead-scoring model was trained in a notebook. Preprocessing ran in a separate cell: median imputation and scaling by hand. The deployment team rewrote the preprocessing from the notebook for production and imputed with the mean. Income was skewed, so the mean was 40% above the median. Scores for every lead with missing income shifted, and the sales team's call list changed without anyone noticing.

A single fitted Pipeline, saved and deployed as one object, leaves no second copy of the preprocessing to get wrong.
